summary: Analysis and source work only; no Lean, no computation. Three corrections to NULL-TRANSFER.md. (1) The claimed iff between 'chi(R^2) <= chi(C\Z)' and EMBEDDABILITY of every finite unit-distance graph is FALSE in the necessity direction: a chromatic supremum does not recover subgraphs. Replaced by the k-dependent criterion: chi(R^2) <= k iff every finite plane unit-distance graph is k-colourable. H is only a sufficient geometric translation criterion; chi(C\Z) = chi(R^2) under H survives as a chromatic statement, not an embedding one. (2) The conclusion produces SOME global colouring and need not extend the supplied one pointwise. (3) A chain is not a strip obstruction - it can be laid flat. Corrected to the fixed strip direction: F translates into a width-w strip iff its perpendicular extent is <= w, and the real obstruction is a RIGID triangulated triangular-lattice patch of side n, every realisation of which contains an equilateral triangle of side n with minimum width n*sqrt3/2. Source packet finished: k_generic_transfer.lean is COMPLETE source (0 elisions), two edits only (Fin 5 -> Fin k; final exact line), imports Converse only (Five unreached), ends with #print axioms. UNCOMPILED, no authority. Accepted family no-go updated to (1/sqrt28, 1/2] per geometry's K7 audit, properness explicit.

verified_results.statement: Correction: the criterion is k-dependent and about colouring, not embedding. chi(R^2) <= k iff every finite unit-distance graph realisable in R^2 is k-colourable (de Bruijn-Erdos, both directions in ZFC). Embeddability of all finite graphs into Gamma(C\Z) is sufficient for 'chi(R^2) <= chi(C\Z)' but NOT necessary, so the earlier iff is withdrawn.
verified_results.grade: PROOF; self-correction of an error in the previous block's STATUS

verified_results.statement: H is only a sufficient geometric criterion, used for exactly one job: making the translation into C\Z work. It is not necessary for the colouring conclusion, and it is not the content of the theorem.
What the conclusion is not: the global colouring produced by the compactness step need not agree with the supplied colouring on C\Z. The lemma asserts existence, not extension.

Strip correction: a configuration F translates into the fixed strip |Im z| <= w/2 iff its perpendicular extent is <= w. A polygonal chain is NOT an obstruction (lay it flat along the axis). The genuine obstruction is a rigid triangulated triangular-lattice patch of side n: it is rigid so all realisations are congruent, each contains an equilateral triangle of side n whose minimum width is n*sqrt3/2, so every realisation has perpendicular extent >= n*sqrt3/2 > w once n > 2w/sqrt3.
verified_results.grade: PROOF; replaces the false diameter-based justification

conjectures: For a domain D the operative sufficient criterion is (H); the sharp question is its failure. For a strip of width w, (H) holds iff every finite unit-distance graph has a realisation of perpendicular extent <= w, which fails first for rigid 2-dimensional patches, not for chains.
chi(C\Z) = chi(R^2) for every null Z is expected (trivial <=, plus <= in the other direction from the transfer under (H)); this is a chromatic equality and involves no embeddability claim.
